headline: Don't plug a power strip into a smart plug — it's a fire risk
summary: Smart plugs have a lower max load capacity than power strips
details: Smart plugs can be convenient, but they should only power one device at a time. The risk of overloading and causing a fire is too great when using a power strip with multiple devices.
The issue is about capacity — smart plugs have a lower maximum load capacity than power strips. If you plug a power strip into a smart plug, you may inadvertently exceed the plug's rated current.
Check your devices' power specifications before plugging them in. Knowing the voltage (V) and wattage (W) — and calculating the maximum amps (A) rating — is crucial for safely managing the load.
TP-Link advises against plugging a power strip into a smart plug, citing the risk of product damage and fire. Save yourself the trouble and plug your power strip directly into the wall.
caption:
Can a smart plug handle a power strip's load?

Smart plugs can be convenient, but they should only power one device at a time. The risk of overloading and causing a fire is too great when using a power strip with multiple devices.

The issue is about capacity — smart plugs have a lower maximum load capacity than power strips. If you plug a power strip into a smart plug, you may inadvertently exceed the plug's rated current.

Check your devices' power specifications before plugging them in. Knowing the voltage (V) and wattage (W) — and calculating the maximum amps (A) rating — is crucial for safely managing the load.

TP-Link advises against plugging a power strip into a smart plug, citing the risk of product damage and fire. Save yourself the trouble and plug your power strip directly into the wall.
